title: Conjecture 1.3
statement_text: For every forest $H$ of maximum degree at most three, MWIS admits a QPTAS and a subexponential-time algorithm in the class of graphs that do not contain any subdivision of $H$ as an induced subgraph.
context_text: In Maximum Weight Independent Set (MWIS), the input is a graph $G$ with a weight function $w:V(G)\to\mathbb{N}$, and one seeks an independent set $X$ maximizing $w(X)=\sum_{x\in X}w(x)$. A QPTAS (quasi-polynomial time approximation scheme) is an algorithm that, given $(G,w)$ and an accuracy parameter $\varepsilon>0$, computes a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation of the optimum in time exponential in a polynomial of $\log|V(G)|$ and $\varepsilon^{-1}$; a subexponential-time algorithm solves the problem exactly in time $2^{o(n)}$ on $n$-vertex graphs. $G$ is $H$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$; a subdivided claw is a subdivision of $K_{1,3}$, and $H$ is treated as a fixed graph (constants may depend on $H$). MWIS is not known to be APX-hard or SUBEXP-hard on $H$-free graphs exactly when every component of $H$ is a path or a subdivided claw, and for all such $H$ the paper gives a QPTAS and an exact algorithm in time $2^{O(|V(G)|^{8/9}\log|V(G)|)}$ on $H$-free graphs. The conjecture generalizes this to excluding all induced subdivisions of a forest of maximum degree at most three. The paper proves it when $H$ is a forest with at most three vertices of degree three (with a $2^{O(|V(G)|^{40/41}\log|V(G)|)}$ subexponential bound); as a side result it also handles graphs with no induced cycle of length at least $t$. The final version of the paper mentions later work (Majewski et al. 2022, Gartland et al.) giving simpler proofs and a quasipolynomial-time exact algorithm when every component of $H$ is a path or a subdivided claw.
paper_title: Quasi-polynomial time approximation schemes for the Maximum Weight Independent Set Problem in H-free graphs
